nativeReference.units: Frontmatter pt values denote native logical points. HTML illustrations use CSS pixels for comparable logical dimensions, not CSS physical points.
nativeReference.appearance: Paired light/dark primitives describe dynamic NSColor tokens. Runtime resolves appearance automatically; previews below illustrate light appearance only.
nativeReference.focus: Runtime focus color comes from NSColor.keyboardFocusIndicatorColor, where individual controls implement focus. Demo Highlight outlines illustrate keyboard focus only.
nativeReference.tonalRamps: Omitted: no eight-step tonal ramp exists in native source. Alpha tints and dynamic appearance pairs must not be presented as synthetic implemented scales.
nativeReference.demoStatus: Every HTML/CSS component below is an illustrative design-panel adapter. None is adopted by SwiftUI/AppKit runtime; web hover/focus rules and SVG marks are not native implementation or native interaction QA.
nativeReference.qa: Twelve AI dock fixture captures cover six states in both appearances. Native keyboard/VoiceOver and whole-app QA remain unverified.

narrative.overview:
Browsemium's native chrome recedes around the page. Compact controls, quiet foreground tints and continuous rounded panels make actions legible without turning the browser into a decorative dashboard. This captures the incumbent SwiftUI/AppKit system; it does not introduce a replacement identity.

The scope is the native macOS application. The source of truth is `Packages/BrowsemiumKit/Sources/BrowsemiumUI/DesignSystem/Theme.swift`, including `BrowserPalette`, `BrowserMetrics` and the shared control views. The site is a separate surface with its own styling. Geist is confirmed for branding and the site; native controls use the macOS system font. The AI dock's composition and approved future work remain in `Plans/7-polished-autonomous-workspace.md`. `PRODUCT.md` governs capability and privacy claims, not layout tokens.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome emphasis with automatic light/dark appearance.
Compact native controls with named actions and explicit state.
Quiet panels, hairline borders and restrained overlay elevation.
Real browser context and honest capability labels.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Keep chrome monochrome except where color names a meaningful status, preserves source identity, or communicates system focus.

rules.name: The Platform Type Rule
rules.body: Keep macOS system type for native controls and reserve bundled Geist for the established wordmark/brand scope.

rules.name: The Quiet Panel Rule
rules.body: Use the incumbent border and tonal layers for ordinary panels; reserve elevation for overlays that already require separation.

dos: Do use the existing dynamic native palette and resolve both appearances.
Do preserve system type, native control semantics and labelled actions.
Do use foreground hierarchy to make tasks and supporting information readable.
Do represent actual context, capabilities and operation state in the interface.
Do adapt content to the available native panel space while keeping actions reachable.
donts: Don't replace the incumbent monochrome identity with a new decorative palette.
Don't apply site typography or site breakpoints to native controls.
Don't add ornamental glow, invented activity or unverifiable counts.
Don't promote the AI dock's local composition into a rule for every surface.
Don't describe approved future automation or fixture inspection as shipped capability or completed native QA.
